source.title: Jo-SNC: Combating Noisy Labels Through Fostering Self- and Neighbor-Consistency
source.authors: Ze-Ren Sun; Ya-Zhou Yao; Tong-Liang Liu; Ze-Chao Li; Fumin Shen; Jin-Hui Tang

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training dynamics on synthetic label noise that bear on V6, but it does not test the original random-label fitting setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior memorization findings, which are not rows. Its own CIFAR80N-O (Sym-20%) training-dynamics results for the Standard method are reported in Figure 4 (bottom) and described in text; those bear on V6. Other noisy-label accuracy results do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: Figure 4 reports Standard training dynamics bearing on V6 in a new open-set setting: true-label accuracy on corrupted ID samples initially increases and subsequently falls nearly to zero as given-label accuracy increases.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' interpretation of Standard's dynamics as early learning of clean patterns followed by noisy-label memorization. The paper's main conclusion is that Jo-SNC improves noisy-label robustness through sample selection, differentiated learning, and consistency regularization.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains noise-robust image classifiers on partially corrupted labels and tracks sample prediction accuracy; it does not use the original random-label fitting intervention.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The relevant dynamics are qualitative figure results for one synthetic noise condition; exact curve values and uncertainty are not stated. The experiment uses partial symmetric label corruption rather than completely random labeling of the full training set.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported accuracy comparisons concern noisy-label robustness rather than the listed claim versions. Figure 5 sample-selection F1 scores and other benchmark test accuracies do not measure the behaviors named by V1–V6.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep from none to all. Benchmark test accuracies alone do not establish this joint claim.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and of removing them on true-label generalization.
Completely random labeling and generality of the learning order across architectures and corruption levels.

record.verdict_notes: Exact curve values and uncertainty for these dynamics cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The robustness methods intentionally alter training to suppress memorization; their performance comparisons do not independently challenge V6.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment fits completely random labels and reports training error and test error.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or sweep of corruption fractions for convergence speed.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep from no corrupted labels to all randomly corrupted labels measuring training fit and test error.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
The dynamics are shown for one synthetic noisy-label setting, not for completely random labels or across multiple corruption levels.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.operation_detail: Tracked prediction accuracy during training for clean samples with respect to their given labels.
rows.measure: Prediction accuracy of clean samples with respect to given labels over training.
rows.value: The text states that prediction accuracy of clean data demonstrably increases during training.
rows.note: Qualitative outcome is described in the text; no exact values are supplied.
rows.check: Clean-label learning is a component of the joint temporal evidence, not sufficient alone to establish learning order. Clarify that Sym-20% denotes corruption within the ID portion; including 20% OOD samples, nominal overall noise is 36%.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.operation_detail: Tracked prediction accuracy during training for ID noisy samples with respect to their given labels.
rows.measure: Prediction accuracy of ID noisy samples with respect to their given, potentially corrupted labels over training.
rows.value: The text states that prediction accuracy of noisy training samples presents a similar trend to clean data.
rows.note: The text describes a similar increasing trend; no exact values are supplied.
rows.check: The text describes noisy samples collectively rather than ID samples specifically; the ID-specific attribution relies on Figure 4. Increasing given-label accuracy supports memorization jointly with R3. Nominal overall noise is 36%, including OOD samples.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.operation_detail: Tracked prediction accuracy during training for ID noisy samples with respect to their ground-truth labels.
rows.measure: Prediction accuracy of ID noisy samples with respect to true labels over training.
rows.value: The text states that accuracy initially increases but then declines to nearly zero.
rows.note: Qualitative outcome is described in the text; no exact values are supplied.
rows.check: The qualitative trajectory is explicitly reported in Section 4.2.2, so evidence_form should include text rather than figure_only. Nominal overall noise is 36%, including OOD samples.

relationships.condition: Standard 7-layer DNN on CIFAR80N-O, Sym-20%, with both ID and OOD noise
relationships.reason: R1–R3 jointly show clean-label learning and increasing fit to supplied noisy labels, while true-label accuracy on corrupted ID samples first increases and then declines nearly to zero.
relationships.display_finding: True-label accuracy on corrupted in-distribution samples initially increased, then declined nearly to zero as fitting of supplied noisy labels increased.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
